# Verification & Closure

`customer_support.diagnosis_and_resolution.verification_and_closure` · v0.1.0 · **draft** · **STUB**

**Is it actually fixed for the person who reported it, and do they say so?**


> Confirming with the person who reported it that the problem has actually stopped, and only then closing. Silence is not agreement — an unanswered "is this resolved?" leaves a ticket unverified rather than verified by default, and auto-closing on silence is the cheapest way ever invented to convert an unmeasured failure into a clean metric. A reopen costs far more than the original contact because it arrives with the customer's patience already spent and their belief that anyone is tracking their problem already damaged, so the whole value of this capability is spending a small confirmation to avoid a large one.

Also write down the reopen taxonomy — never fixed, fixed then regressed, fixed but a second problem, and fixed but the customer disagrees that it should have been the fix — because they carry opposite lessons for Layer 6 and are recorded as one field in every ticketing product on the market.
